options: A new activation function for each layer
How much each weight in the network contributed to the loss, so gradient descent knows which direction to move it
The number of layers a network needs
A replacement for the loss function
questions.explain: Backpropagation finds dL/dw for every weight by applying the chain rule backward from the loss, giving gradient descent the direction to step in.

questions.q: What mathematical rule is backpropagation built on?
options: The chain rule from calculus
Bayes' theorem
The central limit theorem
Linear regression's closed-form solution
questions.explain: Backpropagation is the chain rule applied layer by layer, multiplying derivatives along the path from the loss back to each weight.

questions.q: In the lesson's tiny network, why did dL/dw1 require four multiplied terms while dL/dw2 only required two?
options: w1 was a larger number than w2
The loss function was different for each weight
w1 sits deeper in the network, so the chain rule must pass the error back through the output weight and the hidden activation's derivative first
w2 did not affect the prediction at all
questions.explain: w2 sits right next to the output (2 links). w1 is one layer further back, so its gradient needs two extra links: through w2 and through the hidden neuron's activation derivative.

questions.q: What is a 'numerical gradient', and why did the lesson compute one?
options: A gradient computed by nudging a weight slightly and measuring how much the loss changes, used to double-check the chain-rule result
A random number used to initialize weights
The gradient of the activation function alone
A shortcut that replaces backpropagation entirely
questions.explain: The numerical gradient (loss(w+eps) - loss(w-eps)) / (2*eps) matched the chain-rule derivation to four decimal places, confirming the hand-derived gradients were correct.

questions.q: After one gradient descent step using the computed gradients, what happened to the loss in the lesson's example?
options: It increased
It stayed exactly the same
It became negative
It fell from about 0.1502 to about 0.0858
questions.explain: Stepping each weight against its gradient (scaled by the learning rate) moved the prediction closer to the target and nearly halved the loss.
